## Capital-stock accumulation (module `01_macro`, realization `singleSectorGr`)

The core recursion is `q01_kapMo` (`modules/01_macro/singleSectorGr/equations.gms:120`):

**K(t+1) = K(t)·(1 − δ)^Δt + φ_old(t+1)·I(t) + φ_new(t+1)·I(t+1)**

where:
- `K` = `vm_cesIO(·,·,"kap")` (aggregate capital stock, one of the CES production-function inputs)
- `δ` = `pm_delta_kap(regi,in)` — a constant **annual** depreciation rate per region/capital type
- `Δt = t(t+1) − t(t)` — the (variable) length of the model time step, so depreciation is compounded exponentially over however many years the step spans, not just linearly scaled
- `I(t)` = `vm_invMacro(t,regi,in)` — annual macroeconomic investment flow into the stock
- `φ_old`, `φ_new` = `p01_cumDeprecFactor_old/new` — weights that distribute investment made at the start (`t`) vs. end (`t+1`) of the interval, each discounted by the depreciation they undergo before/after the interval midpoint

**Depreciation-factor construction** (`preloop.gms`): rather than crudely applying `I·Δt` as new capital, REMIND integrates the exponential decay `(1−δ)^s` continuously over the half-step in which each investment vintage is assumed to occur, e.g.

φ_old = [(1−δ)^(Δt/2) − (1−δ)^Δt] / δ
φ_new = [1 − (1−δ)^(Δt/2)] / δ

This is the closed-form of ∫(1−δ)^s ds over the relevant sub-interval, so investment entering mid-step depreciates for only half the step, while investment already present at the start of the step depreciates for the full step. Odd vs. even step lengths (relative to the underlying "counter" resolution) get a slightly adjusted formula with a `1/2` correction term to keep the discretization consistent.

**Net effect:** the stock evolves as *exponential geometric depreciation of the existing stock* plus *investment inflows weighted by how much of the time step they are exposed to depreciation before contributing to next period's stock* — a time-step-length-aware, continuous-time-consistent discretization of the standard `K̇ = I − δK` capital law of motion.

Note: this is the `singleSectorGr` realization (module default); `01_macro/Investment_Inefficiencies` implements a variant with additional inefficiency wedges on top of the same depreciation logic — let me know if you want that one summarized too.
